content.name: Geneviève Tremblay-Ross
content.title: Pharmacy Operations Manager, Primary Care
content.summary: Licensed pharmacist with Additional Prescribing Authorization in Alberta and 16 years across community, long-term care and primary care. I oversee 14 pharmacists embedded in primary care clinics and led a hypertension program that brought 58% of enrolled patients to target within six months.

experience.title: Staff Pharmacist
bullets: Dispensed and counselled on 250–300 prescriptions a day in a high-volume community pharmacy.
Started a blister-pack service for 140 seniors living independently, reducing missed doses reported by home care nurses.
Gave more than 1,500 flu shots each season using Alberta pharmacists' authority to administer injections.

experience.title: Pharmacy Manager
bullets: Managed a team of 4 pharmacists and 6 technicians with annual sales of $5.8 million.
Obtained Additional Prescribing Authorization from the Alberta College of Pharmacy in 2014 and built a prescriber-led renewal and adaptation clinic.
Grew billed comprehensive annual care plans to 900 a year, adding $180,000 in clinical service revenue.
Passed every Alberta College of Pharmacy practice visit with no deficiencies.

experience.title: Consultant Pharmacist, Long-Term Care
bullets: Provided quarterly medication reviews for 620 residents across five continuing care centres.
Cut antipsychotic use without a supporting diagnosis from 24% to 13% of residents through a deprescribing project with physicians and nurses.
Delivered monthly in-services on falls risk medications and anticoagulants to 90 nursing staff.

experience.title: Pharmacy Operations Manager, Primary Care
bullets: Lead 14 pharmacists embedded in 32 family medicine clinics, managing a $2.3 million annual budget.
Launched a pharmacist-led hypertension program for 1,900 patients; 58% reached blood pressure targets within six months.
Introduced a shared documentation template in the clinics' EMR, improving physician acceptance of pharmacist recommendations from 61% to 82%.
Negotiated collaborative practice agreements with 120 physicians and represent pharmacy on the network's quality council.
